kangaroo-at-2024-felix-01.title: Check each number
kangaroo-at-2024-felix-01.body:
- 1 is only in the circle.
- 4 is in the circle and the triangle, but not in the square.
- 5 is in the circle, the square and the triangle. ✓
- 9 is only in the triangle.
- 12 is not in the picture at all.

**Answer: (C) 5**

kangaroo-at-2024-felix-01.title: Where all three overlap
kangaroo-at-2024-felix-01.body:
Find the small region where the circle, the square and the triangle all overlap. The only number in it is 5.

**Answer: (C) 5**

kangaroo-at-2024-felix-02.title: Count the gaps
kangaroo-at-2024-felix-02.body:
All tips are the same size, so compare the wooden parts. Count how many gaps between the vertical lines each one covers:

- A: 5
- B: 7
- C: 6
- D: 8
- E: 7

D is the longest.

**Answer: (D) D**

kangaroo-at-2024-felix-02.title: Compare D and E
kangaroo-at-2024-felix-02.body:
D and E both end far to the right. E ends 2 gaps further right than D, but starts 3 gaps further right, so D is longer by one gap. The others are clearly shorter.

**Answer: (D) D**

kangaroo-at-2024-felix-03.title: Find the pairs
kangaroo-at-2024-felix-03.body:
The faces differ in hat or hair, glasses, ears and mouth. Going through the 15 faces, 7 kinds of face appear twice each. Only one kind appears once: the face with a hat, no glasses, ears and a smile (second row, fourth face).

**Answer: (E)**

kangaroo-at-2024-felix-03.title: Check the choices
kangaroo-at-2024-felix-03.body:
- (A) hair, open mouth, ears: first face in row 2 and last face in row 3.
- (B) hat, glasses, ears: row 1 and row 3.
- (C) hat, glasses, no ears, smile: end of row 2 and start of row 3.
- (D) hair, glasses, no ears: row 1 and row 3.
- (E) hat, no glasses, ears: only once.

**Answer: (E)**

kangaroo-at-2024-felix-04.title: Count the gaps
kangaroo-at-2024-felix-04.body:
Fill in the white part with small triangles in your head: the white space holds 6 small triangles.

**Answer: (B) 6**

kangaroo-at-2024-felix-04.title: Count row by row
kangaroo-at-2024-felix-04.body:
The big triangle has 4 rows with $1 + 3 + 5 + 7 = 16$ small triangles. There are already 10 grey triangles, so $16 - 10 = 6$ are missing.

**Answer: (B) 6**

kangaroo-at-2024-felix-05.title: Count squares of strip
kangaroo-at-2024-felix-05.body:
The strips are 1 square wide. Count how many squares of strip each number uses. A folded corner (shown as a half square) also uses one square of strip.

- 1: 6 squares
- 2: 11 squares
- 5: 11 squares
- 6: 14 squares (the strip crosses itself in the middle)

**Answer: (D) 6**

kangaroo-at-2024-felix-05.title: Compare 5 and 6
kangaroo-at-2024-felix-05.body:
The 2 and the 5 are mirror images, so they are equally long, and the 1 is much shorter. The 6 has the same top part and the same left side as the 5, but it then goes all the way around the bottom loop and back across the middle. So the 6 is the longest.

**Answer: (D) 6**

kangaroo-at-2024-felix-06.title: Mirror left and right
kangaroo-at-2024-felix-06.body:
From outside, left and right are swapped; top and bottom stay the same.

- Top row: black, white, white → white, white, black.
- Middle row: black, black, white → white, black, black.
- Bottom row: white, white, black → black, white, white.

**Answer: (D)**

kangaroo-at-2024-felix-06.title: Look at one corner
kangaroo-at-2024-felix-06.body:
Inside, the bottom right square is black. From outside it must be the bottom left square. Only (D) and (E) have the bottom left square black, and in (E) the top row is wrong.

**Answer: (D)**

kangaroo-at-2024-felix-07.title: Count all toys
kangaroo-at-2024-felix-07.body:
In all 5 baskets together there are 6 ducks, 5 ladybirds, 4 frogs and 5 blue animals.

On the floor there are 6 ducks, 3 ladybirds, 3 frogs and 4 blue animals.

Missing: 2 ladybirds, 1 frog and 1 blue animal. That is basket B.

**Answer: (B) B**

kangaroo-at-2024-felix-07.title: Ladybirds
kangaroo-at-2024-felix-07.body:
Only baskets A, B and D have ladybirds: $1 + 2 + 2 = 5$. On the floor there are 3, so the missing basket has 2 ladybirds: B or D. Basket D has a duck, but all 6 ducks are on the floor. So it is B.

**Answer: (B) B**

kangaroo-at-2024-felix-08.title: Columns first
kangaroo-at-2024-felix-08.body:
- First column: smiley + smiley = 10, so the smiley is 5.
- Third column: heart + heart = 4, so the heart is 2.
- Second column: heart + star = 5, so the star is $5 - 2 = 3$.

**Answer: (C) 3**

kangaroo-at-2024-felix-09.title: Groups of five
kangaroo-at-2024-felix-09.body:
The pictures repeat every 5. After 5 groups, $5 \times 5 = 25$ pictures are drawn. Picture 26 is the 1st picture again (the sun), and picture 27 is the 2nd picture: the ghost.

**Answer: (B)**

kangaroo-at-2024-felix-09.title: Count by fives
kangaroo-at-2024-felix-09.body:
Pictures 1, 6, 11, 16, 21, 26 are all the sun. So picture 27 is the one after the sun: the ghost.

**Answer: (B)**

kangaroo-at-2024-felix-10.title: Smallest and biggest
kangaroo-at-2024-felix-10.body:
The smallest sum is $1 + 2 = 3$, the biggest is $4 + 5 = 9$, and every number in between can be made. From 3 to 9 there are 7 numbers.

**Answer: (C) 7**

kangaroo-at-2024-felix-11.title: Find the columns
kangaroo-at-2024-felix-11.body:
From above Chiara sees a green square wherever at least one small cube stands, no matter how high.

The top layer has cubes along the whole back row (with the marked cube in the corner) and one cube in front of the marked cube, on top of the tall stack. The single cube on the floor stands in the back row too, below the top cubes, so it does not add another green square. The front row is empty.

So she sees the whole back row green and the left square of the middle row green.

**Answer: (E)**

kangaroo-at-2024-felix-11.title: Rule out
kangaroo-at-2024-felix-11.body:
The marked cube and the two cubes next to it on top make the back row green in every picture. The front row has no cubes, so (A) and (B) are wrong. In the middle row only the left square has a cube above it, so (C) and (D) are wrong.

**Answer: (E)**

kangaroo-at-2024-felix-12.title: Check the shared shapes
kangaroo-at-2024-felix-12.body:
Anna and Bella share the square, Anna and Che share the triangle, Bella and Che share the star. Dimitry must share exactly one shape with each of them.

- (A) square, heart, diamond: two shapes with Bella. ✗
- (B) heart, circle, triangle: two shapes with Anna. ✗
- (C) star, diamond, circle: two shapes with Che. ✗
- (D) square, star, triangle: two shapes with Anna. ✗
- (E) diamond, circle, heart: circle with Anna, heart with Bella, diamond with Che. ✓

**Answer: (E)**

kangaroo-at-2024-felix-12.title: Use the unused shapes
kangaroo-at-2024-felix-12.body:
The square, triangle and star are each already shared by two children. If Dimitry had one, he would share two shapes with someone. So he must use the shapes each child has alone: Anna's circle, Bella's heart and Che's diamond.

**Answer: (E)**

kangaroo-at-2024-felix-13.title: Compare towers
kangaroo-at-2024-felix-13.body:
The third tower is the second tower with a pink block added: $20 - 13 = 7$, so the pink block is 7.

First tower: green + pink = 15, so green is $15 - 7 = 8$.

Second tower: roof + green = 13, so the roof is $13 - 8 = 5$.

Fourth tower: roof + pink $= 5 + 7 = 12$.

**Answer: (A) 12**

kangaroo-at-2024-felix-13.title: Take away the green block
kangaroo-at-2024-felix-13.body:
The third tower is roof + pink + green = 20. The fourth tower is the same without the green block. From the first two towers: green = 8. So $20 - 8 = 12$.

**Answer: (A) 12**

kangaroo-at-2024-felix-14.title: Extra arrows
kangaroo-at-2024-felix-14.body:
He threw 20 arrows but started with only 10, so he won $20 - 10 = 10$ extra arrows. Each hit gives 2 arrows: $10 \div 2 = 5$ hits.

**Answer: (B) 5**

kangaroo-at-2024-felix-14.title: Check
kangaroo-at-2024-felix-14.body:
With 5 hits he gets $5 \times 2 = 10$ more arrows: $10 + 10 = 20$ arrows thrown. ✓

**Answer: (B) 5**

kangaroo-at-2024-felix-15.title: Same bridge
kangaroo-at-2024-felix-15.body:
Top picture: 3 cars and $1 + 2 + 1 + 2 = 6$ metres of gaps.

Bottom picture: 2 cars and $4 + 4 + 3 = 11$ metres of gaps.

The bridge is the same, so 3 cars + 6 m = 2 cars + 11 m. One car is $11 - 6 = 5$ metres.

**Answer: (C) 5 metres**

kangaroo-at-2024-felix-15.title: Check
kangaroo-at-2024-felix-15.body:
With 5 m cars: top $15 + 6 = 21$ m, bottom $10 + 11 = 21$ m. ✓

**Answer: (C) 5 metres**
